findings.evidence: maintenance documentation will be supplied and the operating system will be tested
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits which party supplies the maintenance documentation and which party tests the operating system.

findings.evidence: easy of use and compatibility
findings.rationale: Uses subjective, unquantified qualities ('easy of use', 'compatibility') with no measurable criteria.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: The requirement fragment omits the subject/system actor responsible for using the SQL-based database.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: Repeats the SQL-based database requirement already stated in GJ-003 without adding a distinct functional scope.

findings.evidence: Other versions may not be 100% compatible. Also other browsers such as Mozilla or Firefox may not be 100% compatible.
findings.rationale: Uses non-binding 'may not', open-ended 'such as', and unquantified '100% compatible', leaving browser support expectations unclear.

findings.evidence: Compatibility is only tested and verified
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits the actor responsible for testing and verifying browser compatibility.

findings.evidence: Shall install online help for users via the web interface
findings.rationale: The sentence has no subject, leaving unclear which system component or human role performs the installation.

findings.evidence: Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: Syntactic attachment of 'for the Administrator' is ambiguous as to whether it modifies only 'Installation Instructions' or all three documents.

findings.evidence: Shall deliver Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: The sentence omits the subject/actor responsible for delivering the documentation.

findings.evidence: Assume the delivery of development, test and evaluate samples of the USB system from Yoggie.
findings.rationale: Omits the quantity of samples to be delivered and any delivery timeframe, as well as the receiving party.

findings.evidence: freeze the baseline of the USB system after delivery.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which delivery triggers the baseline freeze (sample vs. final delivery) or the timeframe after delivery.

findings.evidence: the system shall be able to be deployed
findings.rationale: Passive construction 'be deployed' does not specify whether deployment happens automatically by the system or is performed by an administrator.

findings.evidence: email customer and vendor in less than 1 second.
findings.rationale: Unclear whether the 1-second limit applies to sending each email individually or both combined, and whether it measures dispatch or delivery.

findings.evidence: The system shall be able to email customer and vendor in less than 1 second.
findings.rationale: Does not specify the triggering event or condition (e.g., order placement) for emailing the customer and vendor.

findings.evidence: validate credit card in less than 2 seconds.
findings.rationale: Specifies credit card validation timing without defining system behavior when the card is invalid, declined, or validation times out.

findings.evidence: acquire shipping charges in less than 2 seconds.
findings.rationale: Relies on acquiring shipping charges without specifying fallback or error handling if retrieval fails or exceeds 2 seconds.

findings.evidence: restore 1000 records per second.
findings.rationale: Omits the triggering condition, backup source, and record scope for the restore operation.

findings.evidence: periodic backups
findings.rationale: 'periodic' is vague and unquantified, giving no testable backup schedule or frequency.

findings.evidence: periodic backups through a live internet connection.
findings.rationale: Omits the numeric interval/unit for backup frequency and specifies no fallback if the live internet connection is unavailable.

findings.evidence: validate credit cards against fraud.
findings.rationale: Lacks measurable criteria or methods defining what constitutes fraud validation.

findings.evidence: validate credit cards against fraud.
findings.rationale: Does not specify what action the system takes when fraud is detected or validation fails.

findings.evidence: all sensitive information
findings.rationale: 'sensitive information' is subjective and undefined without enumerating which data types or fields require HTTPS encryption.

findings.evidence: auto detect IP DOS attacks
findings.rationale: Provides no measurable criteria or traffic pattern definition for what qualifies as an IP DOS attack.

findings.evidence: auto detect IP DOS attacks and block IP automatically.
findings.rationale: Omits both the detection rate threshold and the duration/timeout for which an IP remains blocked.

findings.evidence: detect consecutive failed login attempts.
findings.rationale: Specifies a detection condition without defining either the threshold count of consecutive failed attempts or the resulting system action (e.g., lockout, delay, or alert).

findings.evidence: 'existing' credit card
findings.rationale: Places 'existing' in quotes without defining whether it refers to any stored card, previously used card, or active default card.

findings.evidence: validate 'existing' credit card in system after each log in.
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if the stored credit card fails validation (e.g., expired or invalid) after login.

findings.evidence: too large in size.
findings.rationale: 'too large in size' is subjective and untestable without a defined size threshold.

findings.evidence: compress image files that are too large in size.
findings.rationale: Omits the numeric file-size limit and unit that trigger compression as well as the target compressed size.

findings.evidence: faster execution of pages.
findings.rationale: 'faster' is a comparative, unquantified term with no baseline or measurable page execution target.

findings.evidence: validate email address existence.
findings.rationale: Describes email existence validation without specifying the handling when an address does not exist or cannot be verified.

findings.evidence: easy to use
findings.rationale: 'easy to use' is subjective and lacks measurable usability criteria.

findings.evidence: easy to learn
findings.rationale: 'easy to learn' is subjective and lacks measurable learnability criteria.

findings.evidence: utilize help bubbles to assist managers, customers, and administrators
findings.rationale: Does not specify the UI conditions or interactions that trigger or dismiss help bubbles.

findings.evidence: easy to locate
findings.rationale: 'easy to locate' is subjective and has no measurable layout, contrast, or usability criteria.

findings.evidence: friend easy to read
findings.rationale: 'friend[ly] easy to read' is subjective and untestable without readability or formatting standards.

findings.evidence: prompt customer with friend easy to read error messages.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which error conditions trigger prompts to the customer.

findings.evidence: consistent symbols and colors for clear notifications.
findings.rationale: 'consistent' and 'clear' are subjective and lack a defined visual standard or measurable criteria.

findings.evidence: interchangeable plugins.
findings.rationale: 'interchangeable plugins' is vague without specifying the plugin interface, compatibility standard, or extensible components.

findings.evidence: easily updatable
findings.rationale: 'easily updatable' is subjective and lacks measurable criteria for effort, steps, or downtime.

findings.evidence: easy to upgrade.
findings.rationale: 'easy to upgrade' is subjective and lacks measurable criteria.

findings.evidence: extremely portable
findings.rationale: 'extremely portable' is subjective and unquantified.

findings.evidence: easy to migrate or backed up
findings.rationale: 'easy to migrate' is subjective and untestable, and the coordination leaves unclear whether 'easy to' also applies to 'backed up'.

findings.evidence: should be able to run under debug mode.
findings.rationale: Uses non-mandatory 'should be able to' instead of 'shall', making compliance unclear.

findings.evidence: run under debug mode.
findings.rationale: Does not specify how, when, or by which authorized role debug mode is enabled or disabled.

findings.evidence: should be able to run test credit card transactions.
findings.rationale: Uses non-mandatory 'should be able to' instead of 'shall', making verification optional.

findings.evidence: run test credit card transactions.
findings.rationale: Does not specify the mode or precondition (e.g., test/debug mode only) restricting test credit card transactions.

findings.evidence: should be able to run test shipping orders.
findings.rationale: Uses non-mandatory 'should be able to' instead of 'shall', making verification optional.

findings.evidence: run test shipping orders.
findings.rationale: Does not specify the mode or precondition under which test shipping orders are permitted.

findings.evidence: should be able to create test environment of weborder system.
findings.rationale: Uses non-mandatory 'should be able to' instead of 'shall', making verification optional.

findings.evidence: weborder system.
findings.rationale: Introduces the label 'weborder system' instead of the established product name 'Web Store'.

findings.evidence: The system hardware shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection.
findings.rationale: Passive voice 'shall be fixed and patched' omits who or which component performs the fixing and patching.

findings.evidence: coordinate on future enhancement and features with our organization.
findings.rationale: 'coordinate on future enhancement and features' and 'our organization' are vague and lack concrete scope, obligations, or acceptance criteria.

findings.evidence: OS: Apache web server
findings.rationale: Lists 'Apache web server' as the OS and omits Slackware Linux 2.6, conflicting with GJ-002 which specifies Slackware Linux 2.6 (designed by Yoggie Corporation) as the operating system and Apache Web Server as the web server.
